instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Who Cares More?
cards.instruction: Turn every favor, memory, sacrifice, and affectionate gesture into evidence that you care more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded the corners of all our tickets like yours. Twelve memories carefully marked. How many did you keep?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That corner caught in my zip. I made you an album instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, protect the corners. I've kept your album wrapped in tissue all this time. You made it; I've looked after it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Open it. All my tickets are inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm protecting both collections. I'll get a waterproof cover; you just enjoy remembering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my bag on my head like you. Mine's heavier; I won't let you do more for this picnic than me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was keeping it out of the puddle while I tied my shoe. Put it in the cart.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, keep it dry. I'll push the cart while you rest; I've packed all your favourite food too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then let me push. You've already done the food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me push while you eat. I wrapped your sandwich separately so you wouldn't have to unpack anything.

cards.title: Still a Good Sign
cards.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set my menu aside like you. Our first dinner since the breakup, and we're choosing together already.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's sticky. I want a clean menu, not a reunion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, a clean start. You still tell me exactly what you need; we haven't lost that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to eat without you interpreting everything I say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Comfortable silence, then. We always did that well. I'll order so you can stay quiet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a question mark on Friday like you. Keeping each other guessing. You still make dinner feel like an occasion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means I can't promise. I've cancelled three times already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, no promises. But you're still worrying about letting me down; that's something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop keeping Fridays free for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Looking after my weekends now. I'll make other plans; you always did hate seeing me stuck at home.

cards.title: Affectionate Resentment
cards.instruction: Remain warm and familiar while letting old resentment sharpen beneath every caring gesture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned my cup upside down like yours. Ready for tea, love. I remembered your favourite without a birthday reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's drying. I've brought cake, a month late, I know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, let it dry. I'll warm you a plate for the cake; I've kept the candle ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put it in. I'll sing now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come closer, love. I'll shield the flame so we get further than last year's birthday phone call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my socks on the radiator like yours. Warming a pair for each other, love. No forty-minute wait from me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are drying for me to wear. I said sorry about leaving you outside the office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, properly dry first. Take my warm socks; I wouldn't want you feeling forgotten as well as cold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're too small. Could you just warm my feet with yours?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come here, love. Both feet. I won't leave one outside while I finish a meeting.

cards.title: Relationship Ledger
cards.instruction: Price closeness, forgiveness, and support in favors, sacrifices, access, and future loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked my opening invitation like you did. Two yeses. Come along and I'll forgive our argument.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ticked yours because I'd checked the address. I work that night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, address checked. You know where to bring the apology, then. Could you help hang the paintings instead?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can hang them on Sunday. I can't stay all day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hanging gets you forgiven. Stay for tea and I won't retell the argument to Mum.

beats.text: I've tied a ribbon on the spare key like yours. A little gift, for one Saturday lunch with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine marks the storage cupboard. I need the sitting-room key to collect my records.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, separate access. Lunch buys the sitting room; I'll have the records ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring enough for both of us. Then I need to carry the boxes to the car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lunch gets you the records. Listen to one with me and I'll help with the boxes.

cards.title: Closer on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to repair the relationship while redefining closeness around the boundaries that benefit you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've closed my menu like you. Dinner sorted. Yes, let's reconnect, but I'll leave at ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I closed it because I forgot my reading glasses. We haven't ordered, let alone talked about why you left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, we'll order together. Tell me the difficult part before pudding so we can finish nicely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if I'm still upset at ten?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll book another dinner. I'll keep coming, but I want a finishing time each night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed out Sunday on the hotel form like you. Flexible weekends; lovely. Saturday will be plenty of time to patch things up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sunday's fully booked. Saturday still needs to include the arguments we've been avoiding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, one day at a time. Let's have a pleasant afternoon first, then you can tell me what still needs discussing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That leaves hardly any time. I've got a lot to say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Email me the rest. I'll read it when I'm ready; let's keep the afternoon for enjoying each other.
